title: Tenali Raman and the Miraculous Nostrum

full_text:
A charismatic traveling charlatan named Hakim Dhanvantari arrived in Vijayanagara, selling bottles of a cloudy, foul-smelling dark liquid he called the 'Universal Elixir of Ten Thousand Herbs'.
He claimed: 'A single spoonful of this elixir cures blindness, baldness, rheumatism, asthma, broken bones, and guarantees a life of one hundred and fifty years!'
He charged ten silver coins per bottle, fleecing hundreds of poor, sick villagers.

Tenali Raman resolved to expose the fraud before the public.

Tenali dressed in the ragged clothes of a crippled beggar, limping heavily with two crutches, his face smeared with ash, groaning piteously as he dragged himself to the Hakim’s booth in the central bazaar.
A large crowd gathered.

Tenali groaned:
'O Great Hakim! I have been crippled in both legs for twenty years! I cannot take a single step without these crutches!
Can your miraculous elixir heal my legs right now?'

The Hakim, eager to demonstrate a theatrical 'miracle' before hundreds of paying customers, boasted loudly:
'Drink this bottle, brother! In one minute, thy legs will run like a mountain gazelle!'

Tenali drank the bottle, smacked his lips, and blinked.
Then Tenali looked at the Hakim with an expression of sudden, intense demonic fury!
Tenali raised his heavy wooden crutches in the air, shouted at the top of his lungs:
'Help! This man has given me demon’s poison! It has turned me into a wild madman!'
Tenali began swinging his heavy crutches like war clubs directly at the Hakim’s head!
*SWISH! CRACK!*

The terrified Hakim shrieked in terror, leaped over his display table, dropped his bottles, and began running for his life down the crowded bazaar!
Tenali ran right behind him, sprinting with the speed of an Olympic athlete, brandishing his crutches, shouting:
'Halt, Hakim! Let me thank thee with my crutches!'

The Hakim ran three laps around the temple square, gasping for breath, dodging cows and carts, before diving headfirst into an open mud ditch, screaming:
'Help! Police! Save me from this madman!'

Tenali stopped at the edge of the ditch, tossed aside his crutches, and laughed heartily before the cheering crowd:
'Look at the great Hakim!
He promised his medicine would make a crippled man run like a gazelle—and indeed, it made the Hakim himself run like a gazelle through the mud!'

Tenali then revealed the contents of the bottles: common pond water mixed with bitter neem juice, molasses, and dirt!
The charlatan was marched out of the city gates, and Tenali was hailed as the protector of public health and common sense.
moral: Quack doctors who sell fake cures for profit are silenced when forced to drink their own concoctions.
